_meta.indication: GEMTESA is indicated for the treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo- and active (tolterodine)-controlled, 12-week study; patients randomized 5:5:4 to vibegron 75 mg, placebo, or tolterodine ER 4 mg once daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with symptoms of overactive bladder for at least 3 months and ≥8 micturitions per diary day.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline at Week 12 in average number of micturitions per 24 hours (all OAB patients) and in average number of urge urinary incontinence (UUI) episodes per 24 hours (OAB Wet patients).
pivotal_trials.n: N=1518 randomized (placebo 540, vibegron 75 mg 547, tolterodine ER 4 mg 431).
pivotal_trials.result: Micturitions: difference from placebo -0.5 (95% CI -0.8, -0.2; p<0.001). UUI episodes: difference from placebo -0.6 (95% CI -0.9, -0.3; p<0.0001). Both co-primary endpoints met.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) were headache (4.0% vs 2.4% placebo), urinary tract infection, nasopharyngitis (2.8% vs 1.7%), diarrhea (2.2% vs 1.1%), nausea (2.2% vs 1.1%), and upper respiratory tract infection (2.0% vs 0.7%). Urinary retention is the identified warning.
target_moa: Vibegron is a selective human beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist; activation of the beta-3 adrenergic receptor increases bladder capacity by relaxing the detrusor smooth muscle during bladder filling.

rems.type: DRM along with DUOG agreed that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of vibegron outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

description.text: Expanded to include treatment of OAB in adult males on pharmacological therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency in adult males on pharmacological therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

summary.text: GEMTESA (vibegron) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity and reviewed under Standard (non-priority) review; it received a full (traditional) approval based on the placebo-controlled Study 3003, with no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority designations noted.

citations.quote: *“As amended, Urovant Sciences’ 505(b)(1) New Drug Application 213006 for GEMTESA (vibegron) tablets, 75 mg, is recommended for APPROVAL from the OPQ perspective.*
Vibegron is a new molecular entity (NME), not currently marketed in the US.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric trial (#3991-1): a sequential cohort, vibegron dose-modification trial to determine the multiple-dose pharmacokinetics, safety and efficacy of vibegron in the treatment of pediatric patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity aged 3 to less than 17 years.
